title: `sum` of floats: pairwise, Kahan when grouped
verdict: pairwise (full); Kahan (grouped, in memory); in turn (grouped, streaming); in the input's width
description: A full aggregation sums pairwise: blocks of 128 in 16 SIMD stripes, combined pairwise, the remainder added in turn. Groups of indices use Kahan summation with a finiteness guard. Streaming merges partial sums plainly.
The sum of no values (or only nulls) is 0 in the Series API.

The sum has the input's width. A `Float32` column adds in single precision on every path: `sum_arr_as_f32` with `f32` lanes, `KahanSum<f32>` per group, `NumSumReducer<Float32Type>` (`SumCast` maps `f32` to `f32`). One `Float32` group of 16777216, 1, 1 sums to 16777216 ungrouped and grouped when streaming, and to 16777218 grouped in memory (Kahan). Each step is one IEEE addition, rounded to nearest with ties to even; the paths differ in the order of the additions. The float-sum kernel uses plain `+`, not the reassociable `alg_add_f64`.

Streaming engine (a lazy `collect()` by default, polars-exec-engine): ungrouped, each morsel is summed by the in-memory kernel (`ChunkAgg::sum`, pairwise per chunk), added to its pipeline's running sum, and the pipelines' sums are added in pipeline order. Which morsels a pipeline receives depends on scheduling, so the grouping of a large sum can change between runs. Grouped, each value is added in turn to its group's sum (`reduce_one`, `+=`) and the pipelines' partial sums are added on merge. So grouped sums differ between the engines: Kahan in memory, plain left-to-right when streaming. One `Float64` group of 1e16, 1, 1, -1e16 sums to 2.0 in memory and 0.0 streaming.
reference: `AggFn.fsum` (`floatSum`) adds the doubles one by one in list order from +0.0; the writers that need that order exactly use `Dialect.float_sum`. NULL without values.

evidence.note: `SumCast`: `f32` and `f64` sum in their own type
per-array sum: `sum_arr_as_f32` for `f32`, `sum_arr_as_f64` for `f64`; chunks folded left
SIMD block sum: 16 lanes of the output type, then `vector_horizontal_sum`
pairwise main part plus the remainder added in turn
Kahan step; the error term is kept only while finite
ungrouped streaming reduce: each pipeline folds its morsels into a local state (`update_group`), the local states merge in pipeline order (`combine_subset`)
`VecGroupedReduction`: `update_group` calls `reduce_ca` on a morsel; `update_groups_subset` calls `reduce_one` per row
streaming group_by: each pipeline updates its local per-group states row by row
the pipelines' pre-aggregated states merge with `combine_subset`

provenance.notes: Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine has its own reducers in `polars-expr/src/reduce`, lowered by `polars-stream`; sums of `Float32` and `Float64` take the same generic code.

evidence.note: pl.LazyFrame({'g': [1]*3, 'x': [16777216.0, 1.0, 1.0]}, schema={'g': pl.Int64, 'x': pl.Float32}): select(x.sum()) is 16777216.0 on both engines; group_by('g').agg(x.sum()) is 16777218.0 in memory and 16777216.0 streaming
pl.LazyFrame({'g': [1]*4, 'x': [1e16, 1.0, 1.0, -1e16]}): group_by('g').agg(x.sum()) is 2.0 in memory and 0.0 streaming; select(x.sum()) is 0.0 on both

provenance.notes: Polars 2.1.0 (Python) from the project's environment, macOS arm64, `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=2`; each `LazyFrame` collected with `engine="in-memory"` and `engine="streaming"`.
